Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberShield Second Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star one to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberShield's results for the second quarter fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer; Chris Novak, VP of Sales; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; and Ryan Desai, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Emily, and good afternoon, everyone. CyberShield delivered exceptional results in the second quarter, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. Our performance reflects the strength of our product portfolio, our expanding customer base, and our commitment to innovation. The adoption rate of ShieldXDR is accelerating, demonstrating its transformative impact and the value we bring to our customers.

As we dive deeper into our Q2 results, I want to highlight our recent product and feature launches, which have been pivotal in driving our record 42% year-over-year revenue growth to $285 million and expanding our annual recurring revenue, or ARR, to $1.12 billion—up 38% from the prior year. These innovations are squarely addressing the cybersecurity industry's seismic shifts: the explosion of GenAI-driven threats, a 65% surge in ransomware-as-a-service attacks per our latest threat intelligence report—mirroring Chainalysis data—and the relentless push toward zero-trust architectures amid hybrid cloud adoption. Gartner projects the endpoint detection and response, or EDR, market to hit $12 billion by 2027, and we're capturing meaningful share through our launches.

Let me start with ShieldXDR 2.5, our next-gen extended detection and response platform, which we rolled out in April. This is a game-changer in unified threat management. Building on our existing XDR foundation—already powering 4,500 enterprise customers—we've integrated autonomous GenAI agents for real-time threat hunting and behavioral anomaly detection. Using proprietary large language models fine-tuned on 15 petabytes of anonymized telemetry from our global sensor network, ShieldXDR 2.5 achieves 98.7% accuracy in predicting zero-day exploits, a 25% improvement over our prior version and outperforming CrowdStrike Falcon's Insight XDR in independent AV-TEST benchmarks from Q1.

The numbers speak for themselves: Since launch, we've seen 1,200 net-new deployments, contributing $18 million in Q2 bookings—150% above our internal forecast—and boosting our XDR ARR to $420 million, up 55% YoY. Customer wins include a Fortune 50 financial services firm migrating from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, citing our 40% faster mean-time-to-response, or MTTR, at under 5 minutes. Strategically, this positions us as the XDR leader for mid-market enterprises underserved by pricier incumbents like Palo Alto's Cortex XDR, where we're pricing 20-30% more competitively at $45 per endpoint per month.

Next, NexTrust Edge, our cloud-native Secure Access Service Edge, or SASE, solution launched in May. In a world where 75% of organizations are now multi-cloud per Flexera's 2024 State of the Cloud Report, traditional VPNs are obsolete. NexTrust Edge delivers zero-trust network access, or ZTNA, with inline deep packet inspection and SWG—secure web gateway—capabilities, all orchestrated via our Kubernetes-native control plane. Key features include adaptive access policies powered by UEBA, or user and entity behavior analytics, which reduced unauthorized access attempts by 62% in early pilots, and integration with AWS Nitro Enclaves for confidential computing to meet stringent data sovereignty regs like GDPR and Brazil's LGPD.

Adoption has been explosive: 850 customers onboarded in Q2, driving $12 million in new ARR and representing 22% of our total bookings. Regionally, this is our breakout star—EMEA grew 68% quarter-over-quarter thanks to DORA compliance deadlines, with wins at three top-10 European banks. In APAC, we're up 82%, fueled by Singapore's cybersecurity levy and Australia's Essential Eight framework; we've secured partnerships with telcos like Singtel, expanding our footprint to 1,200 endpoints across ASEAN. Compared to Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange, our edge compute latency is sub-50ms globally, giving us a clear advantage in high-latency regions.

Finally, a quick note on QuantumShield, our post-quantum cryptography feature set, generally available in June as an add-on to our endpoint portfolio. With NIST's first standardized PQC algorithms now live and IBM warning of harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks, we've embedded Kyber and Dilithium lattice-based crypto into our TLS 1.3 stack, ensuring forward secrecy for all traffic. Early uptake: 40% attach rate among existing customers, adding $5 million in upsell revenue, with pilots at U.S. defense contractors ahead of the 2025 DoD mandate.

These launches aren't just products—they're our strategic moat. We've invested $150 million in R&D this year, 28% of revenue, focusing on AI ops and autonomous SOCs to counter the talent shortage, where McKinsey estimates a 3.5 million global shortfall. Against a frothy M&A backdrop—witness Broadcom's $61 billion VMware deal reshaping SASE dynamics—we're accelerating inorganic growth, with two tuck-in acquisitions in stealth for UEBA and deception tech. Looking ahead, we guide Q3 new product bookings at $50-55 million, with ShieldXDR and NexTrust Edge comprising 70%.

Our strategic priorities are focused on eight key areas: advancing recent product and feature launches like ShieldXDR and NexTrust Edge, optimizing performance across key product lines such as cloud security and SASE, providing a strong full-year revenue and profitability outlook, scaling the number of new customers acquired, driving expansion within existing large accounts, boosting platform adoption over point products, maintaining low churn rates through proactive measures, and clearly articulating the assumptions underlying our guidance.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. We achieved record revenue of $285 million in the second quarter, representing a 42% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained strong at 81%, and we continued to invest in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $220 million. Net income was $55 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.42. We are increasing our full-year revenue and earnings guidance to $1.05 billion to $1.08 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.85 to $1.95 based on our strong performance to date.

I'll now dive into the performance of our core product lines, with a particular focus on Cloud Security and SASE, which together accounted for approximately 65% of our total Q2 ARR of $1.12 billion, up 38% year-over-year. These segments continue to outperform the broader cybersecurity market, which Gartner projects to grow at a 14.4% CAGR through 2027, driven by accelerating cloud migrations and the convergence of networking and security under zero-trust architectures.

Our Cloud Security portfolio, encompassing our CNAPP—Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform—solution built on our proprietary CloudGuard engine, delivered exceptional results this quarter. Revenue reached $480 million in Q2, representing 40% of total revenue and surging 52% year-over-year, outpacing the 35-40% growth we've guided for the full year. ARR for this line hit $1.85 billion, with dollar-based net retention—DBNR—expanding to 128%, reflecting strong multi-workload expansions among our top 500 customers.

Key drivers included a 65% increase in net new ARR from large enterprises, fueled by our recent launch of AI-driven Cloud Workload Protection—and CWP—and Cloud Security Posture Management—or CSPM—modules. For instance, our GenAI-powered anomaly detection, which leverages reinforcement learning to identify zero-day misconfigurations in real-time—reducing mean time to remediate, or MTTR, by 40% in beta trials—secured wins with three Fortune 50 financial services firms. We've also deepened integrations with AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Google Cloud's Vertex AI, enabling seamless shift-left security for DevSecOps pipelines. This addresses the surging demand post high-profile incidents like the Change Healthcare ransomware attack, where cloud exposure amplified breach costs averaging $4.88 million per IBM's latest Cost of a Data Breach report.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse at 62% of Cloud Security ARR, with expansions into multi-cloud environments boosting average contract value, or ACV, by 22% to $1.2 million. EMEA grew 48% YoY, propelled by GDPR and CCPA compliance mandates and wins in the DACH region, while APAC exploded 75% YoY—led by Japan and Singapore hyperscaler deals amid rising state-sponsored threats like those from Volt Typhoon, as flagged by CISA. Churn remains sub-2%, underscoring sticky adoption as customers consolidate point solutions; our CNAPP now protects over 2.5 million Kubernetes clusters globally, positioning us neck-and-neck with Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud in IDC's latest Cloud-Native Security tracker.

Strategically, we're investing 15% of R&D into agentless CSPM enhancements and runtime behavioral analytics, targeting a $25 billion TAM by 2028 per McKinsey. Cross-sell into our SASE suite yielded a 35% attach rate, creating a flywheel effect.

Shifting to SASE, our unified SSE—Security Service Edge—platform—including ZTNA, CASB, SWG, and integrated SD-WAN—posted $300 million in Q2 revenue, up 61% YoY and comprising 25% of total revenue. ARR climbed to $1.1 billion, with DBNR at 122% and a net promoter score, or NPS, of 68, reflecting the platform's edge in delivering sub-50ms latency for secure remote access.

This quarter's highlights included 140 net new logos, 40% of which were six-figure deals, driven by our SASE 3.0 update featuring ML-optimized traffic steering and inline DLP—Data Loss Prevention—that blocks 99.9% of shadow IT exfiltration attempts. A standout was a $45 million multi-year contract with a global telco, migrating from legacy VPNs to our ZTNA fabric, which reduced their attack surface by 70% per independent penetration testing. We've also embedded post-quantum cryptography readiness, ahead of NIST's curve, to future-proof against harvest-now-decrypt-later threats.

Market tailwinds are undeniable: Post-pandemic hybrid work has ballooned the SASE TAM to $40 billion by 2028 per Forrester, with SD-WAN convergence accelerating adoption. Our platform's single-pane-of-glass management has eroded shares from siloed players like Zscaler and Cisco Umbrella, capturing 12% mindshare in G2's Fall 2024 Grid report.

Geographically, EMEA led with 55% YoY growth to 28% of SASE ARR, boosted by NIS2 Directive compliance and partnerships with Vodafone and BT; North America held steady at 52%, with federal wins via our FedRAMP High authorization. APAC, at 20%, surged 82% on ANZ banking deals and India's DPDP Act rollout, though we note pricing pressures in cost-sensitive LATAM, where we're piloting bundled offerings.

Looking ahead, our roadmap emphasizes SASE orchestration with 5G edge computing and sovereign cloud support—think integrations with Oracle Cloud and Alibaba—aiming for 50%+ YoY growth in FY25. We've seen 28% quarter-over-quarter upsell from Cloud Security customers, validating our "security everywhere" vision.

In summary, Cloud Security and SASE are not just growing—they're redefining our competitive moat in a market where 85% of breaches involve cloud assets per Palo Alto's 2024 Unit 42 report. With $750 million in remaining performance obligations, or RPO, billings up 38% to $320 million, and a 115% Rule of 40 score, these lines position CyberShield for sustained 30%+ revenue growth. We're allocating $250 million in FY25 capex to scale our global PoPs to 150 and advance autonomous security operations.

Turning to new customer acquisition, one of our key growth drivers, in Q2 we acquired 452 new customers, marking a robust 38% year-over-year increase from the 327 wins in Q2 2023, and a solid 14% quarter-over-quarter growth from the 397 in Q1 2024. This performance outpaced our internal guidance of 10-12% QoQ growth and underscores the momentum behind our platform-centric strategy. For context, our total customer base now stands at approximately 4,200, with net revenue retention holding steady at 118%, driven by upsell opportunities in our XDR and Zero Trust modules.

Breaking this down by segment: Enterprise wins—defined as ARR greater than $100K—we landed 128 new logos, up 42% YoY and 18% QoQ. Notable wins included a top-5 global bank adopting our CyberShield XDR platform to consolidate their fragmented SIEM and EDR tools—replacing a legacy setup from Splunk and CrowdStrike Falcon—and a Fortune 100 healthcare provider integrating our SASE solution amid the fallout from the Change Healthcare breach. These deals averaged $450K in initial ARR, with multi-year contracts featuring our new AI-Driven Behavioral Analytics engine, which reduced false positives by 65% in beta testing.

Commercial and SMB segments—ARR $10K-$100K—added 324 customers, a 36% YoY surge, fueled by our channel partnerships with over 1,200 MSSPs worldwide. This includes expansions with distributors like Ingram Micro, penetrating mid-market verticals such as manufacturing and retail, where vulnerability exploitation rates spiked 30% due to unpatched OT/IoT devices. Our SMB-focused CyberShield Essentials bundle, priced at $5/user/month, saw 55% adoption among these wins, emphasizing cloud-native endpoint protection with built-in DLP.

Regionally: North America at 60% of new wins, or 271 customers, with 22% YoY growth driven by hyperscaler integrations like AWS GuardDuty and Azure Sentinel connectors. EMEA 25%, 113 customers, up 52% on NIS2 compliance; APAC 15%, 68 customers, up 65% amid ransomware surges.

These wins stem from AI/ML innovations like our GenAI Threat Fusion engine, ecosystem expansions with ServiceNow and Zscaler, and go-to-market shifts like product-led growth converting 28% of pilots. We're guiding 500-550 new customers in Q3.

On expansion within existing large accounts—those generating over $1 million in ARR, now 68% of our total ARR base—this segment contributed 42% of our overall ARR growth, or $28.4 million in net new expansion revenue. Our DBNR for large accounts hit 128% in Q2, ahead of peers, with existing customer expansion accounting for 112% and renewals 16%. Churn under 1.2%.

Drivers include land-and-expand: 73% of top 50 accounts adopted full-stack CyberMesh SASE. Example: GlobalBank Corp. grew ACV from $4.2M to $7.8M with ForgeAI detecting ransomware in 14 minutes. North America 135% DBNR, EMEA 122%, APAC 118%. This validates platformization, with gen-AI expansions and 88% gross margins on expansions.

Regarding platform adoption versus point products, in Q2 platform adoption accounted for 68% of total net new ARR, up from 52% YoY, while point products dropped to 32%. Platform cohort NRR 128% vs. 112% for points. RPO from platforms 72%. Our SecureNet One-like architecture ingests 10 trillion events daily, with GenAI achieving 98.7% MTTD. CNAPP launch reduced cloud attack surface 62%. North America 72% of wins, EMEA 55% YoY. Expect 75% by year-end.

On churn, our gross dollar-based churn was 7.2% in Q2, down 400 bps YoY, with NRR at 118%. Voluntary churn 4.8%: M&A 22%, budgets 35%, competition 18%. Involuntary 2.4%. North America 6.1%, EMEA 9.4%, APAC 7.8%. Initiatives: GenAI threat hunting, CSAT incentives, churn prediction.

For full-year outlook, we're raising revenue guidance to $1.05B-$1.08B, 25-28% growth. Subscription 27-30%, ARR $1.12B-$1.15B. Americas 60%, EMEA 25%, APAC 15%. Non-GAAP op margins 28-30%, EPS $1.85-$1.95, FCF $350M.

Assumptions: 13.5% market CAGR, NRR 118%, Americas 62%, EMEA NIS2 uplift, APAC 28%. Product roadmap on-time, stable macros, no recession.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for Q&A session. Thank you. First question comes from Mike Rossi with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Rossi: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Can you expand on the assumptions behind the raised guidance, particularly around customer metrics and regional growth?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, Mike. Our guidance assumes NRR at 118%, with 92% gross retention and 28% expansions. Large enterprise win rates over 45%, SMB 15% sequential. Americas 62% of growth on federal and vertical demand, EMEA 24% on NIS2, APAC 14% on DPDPA. Cloud-native 55% of bookings, stable IT budgets. We've stress-tested for macro pressures.

Operator: Next question comes from Sarah Lin with Morgan Stanley.

Sarah Lin: Great, thanks. On churn, what are the main reasons and how are you addressing them?

Jordan Lee: Sarah, churn at 7.2%, best in years. Voluntary from M&A, budgets, competition; involuntary non-payment. Product-led retention with GenAI, customer success overhauls, GTM refinements. Outperforms industry at 10-12%.

Operator: Next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan.

David Patel: Alex or Taylor, thoughts on platform adoption versus points and tech roadmap?

Taylor Kim: Thanks, David. Platform at 68% of net new ARR, NRR 128%. Architecture handles 10T events, GenAI 98.7% accuracy. Q3: Autonomous SOC beta, Snowflake integrations. Driving 42-45% ARR growth.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Grant with Barclays.

Lisa Grant: Jordan, details on new customer adds and expansions in large accounts?

Jordan Lee: Lisa, 452 new customers, 38% YoY: 128 enterprise, 324 commercial/SMB. Regions strong. Large accounts DBNR 128%, 42% of growth, expansions margin-accretive at 88% gross.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create value for our shareholders. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners.

Emily Carter: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
